subject: Materials Science
title: Carburization and Sulfidation
description: A fast breakdown of Carburization and Sulfidation for builders.

hook.text: In a petrochemical furnace, carbon from cracked hydrocarbons diffuses into the steel wall — making it brittle.

buildup.text: Carburization occurs when carbon-rich gases at high temperature diffuse into alloys, forming carbides.

discovery.text: Sulfidation attacks when sulfur compounds replace oxygen — sulfide scales grow ten times faster than oxides.

twist.text: Nickel resists carburization but is devastated by sulfidation — no single alloy handles all environments.

climax.text: Ethylene cracking furnace tubes are made from 35Ni-25Cr alloys designed specifically to resist carburization.

punchline.text: At extreme temperatures, even the atmosphere passing through an alloy matters.

quiz.question: What makes sulfidation more aggressive than oxidation?
options: Sulfide scales are thinner and more protective
Sulfide scales grow much faster than oxide scales
Sulfur atoms are larger and cannot penetrate metals
